about: The top tier of the library, scored on two separate axes per ChatGPT's recommendation: originality (does it introduce a distinctive governing idea, input→output relationship or navigation model? 1-5) and transfer (how well the idea carries to the personal site of a backend/systems engineer who runs pre-registered research, 1-5). Discoverability is deliberately NOT a factor. Every entry states what the visitor does, what changes, and what it reveals. mechanic_basis: 'sweep' = from a research sweep's source description; 'observed' = from our own first-frame captures; 'reported' = from an agent's report of the site.

tiers.group: Executable argument — the claim is something you run

sites.name: Explorable Multiverse Analyses
sites.mechanic: The visitor switches an analysis choice in the text, causing the reported statistics to change, which reveals how robust or fragile the finding is.
sites.why: The closest existing interface to pre-registration and keeping failures on the record.

sites.name: The Secret Lives of Data: Raft
sites.mechanic: The visitor clicks nodes to stop them or send requests, causing elections and log replication to play out, which reveals how Raft reaches agreement under failure.
sites.why: A distributed-systems guarantee made watchable; the template for explaining correctness under failure.

sites.name: samwho — Load Balancing
sites.mechanic: The visitor changes the algorithm and request rate, causing queues and latency percentiles to shift, which reveals why naive round-robin fails under uneven load.
sites.why: Backend behaviour under load as a live simulation, written for engineers.

sites.name: Numbers Every Programmer Should Know, by Year
sites.mechanic: The visitor drags the year slider, causing each latency figure and bar to update, which reveals which hardware costs fell and which barely moved.
sites.why: One slider turns a famous table into an argument about time.

sites.name: Tangle (Bret Victor)
sites.mechanic: The visitor drags a number inside a sentence, causing dependent values and charts to recalculate, which reveals the model behind the prose.
sites.why: Reactive documents: numbers in a write-up you can push to see the trade-off.

sites.name: Nutshell (Nicky Case)
sites.mechanic: The visitor clicks a highlighted phrase, causing the explanation to unfold in place, which reveals depth on demand without leaving the page.
sites.why: Lets a short case study carry its full technical depth.

sites.name: The Evolution of Trust
sites.mechanic: The visitor plays rounds and edits payoffs and noise, causing populations of strategies to rise or collapse, which reveals when cooperation survives.
sites.why: A falsifiable claim presented as an experiment the visitor runs.

sites.name: Why Momentum Really Works (Distill)
sites.mechanic: The visitor drags momentum and step-size sliders, causing the optimiser's path to oscillate or converge, which reveals its stability regions.
sites.why: Research rigour and explanatory interface without either compromising.

sites.name: Is Twitter Throttling a Website Right Now? (The Markup)
sites.mechanic: The visitor runs the test on their own connection, causing requests to different domains to be timed, which reveals whether links are delayed.
sites.why: Evidence the reader produces, not evidence they're shown.

tiers.group: The running system is the interface

sites.name: Perfetto UI
sites.mechanic: The visitor drops a trace and brushes a time range, causing aggregations and SQL results to recompute for that slice, which reveals where time actually went.
sites.why: The best interface for a system's causal and temporal structure; directly a backend engineer's world.

sites.name: speedscope
sites.mechanic: The visitor flips between time-order, left-heavy and sandwich views, causing the same samples to re-aggregate, which reveals different truths about one profile.
sites.why: One dataset, several honest views — a model for presenting performance results.

sites.name: Low-tech Magazine (solar)
sites.mechanic: The visitor loads the page, causing the header battery gauge to show the solar server's charge, which reveals that the site's availability depends on the weather.
sites.why: Infrastructure as the argument; the constraint is the identity.

sites.name: earth.nullschool.net
sites.mechanic: The visitor spins the globe and picks an overlay, causing particles and colour to switch layers, which reveals live global weather.
sites.why: A living instrument as visual identity, with no decorative animation.

sites.name: LLM Visualization (Brendan Bycroft)
sites.mechanic: The visitor flies through the model and clicks a block, causing its tensor shapes and values to be explained in place, which reveals how inference flows.
sites.why: A whole system rendered spatially and inspectable — the honest version of a '3D portfolio scene'.

sites.name: Exposing Floating Point (Ciechanowski)
sites.mechanic: The visitor flips sign, exponent and mantissa bits, causing the value to change, which reveals rounding and precision.
sites.why: Ciechanowski's method — mechanism first, never simplified — applied to a programmer's daily material.

tiers.group: One governing fiction — personal sites built on a single idea

sites.name: Bruno Simon
sites.mechanic: The visitor drives a toy car around a 3D map, causing project areas to be reached, which reveals the work.
sites.why: The canonical single-fiction portfolio. Blank in software GL — a lesson in fallback as much as in concept.

sites.name: Henry Heffernan
sites.mechanic: The visitor boots a fake BIOS and the camera dives into a 3D computer, causing a desktop OS to become the navigation, which reveals the portfolio as an environment.
sites.why: The loading screen is part of the fiction — the best answer to 'loader as first frame'.

sites.name: Nicolás Zarcero — Box Office
sites.mechanic: The visitor chooses a window at an illustrated cinema box office, causing a five-act portfolio to begin, which reveals the work as a programme with an intermission.
sites.why: The strongest first frame in the audit, with no GPU needed: the concept reads in one look.

sites.name: Lynn Fisher
sites.mechanic: The visitor returns each year, causing a wholly new site concept to appear with the archive intact, which reveals a personal site as an annual practice.
sites.why: Iteration as identity — matches a person who keeps every experiment on the record.

sites.name: Maggie Appleton — Digital Garden
sites.mechanic: The visitor browses notes tagged by growth stage, causing seedlings, budding notes and evergreen essays to sit side by side, which reveals thinking in progress.
sites.why: A legitimate way to publish unfinished research without pretending it's finished.

sites.name: Andy Matuschak's notes
sites.mechanic: The visitor clicks a note link, causing the next note to stack alongside, which reveals the web of ideas behind the work.
sites.why: A thinking environment instead of a portfolio.

sites.name: Messenger (abeto)
sites.mechanic: The visitor walks a small 3D planet, causing other live visitors and NPCs to appear, which reveals presence as the content.
sites.why: 2025 Developer Site of the Year; shared presence over WebSockets is the idea.

sites.name: rmv.fyi
sites.mechanic: The visitor drags across a pasteboard, causing work, software and essays to slide into view, which reveals a body of work as objects on a desk.
sites.why: A spatial index without 3D.

sites.name: Carter Ogunsola
sites.mechanic: The visitor moves across a dark canvas of scattered, labelled project cards, causing a 'View project' cursor to lock on, which reveals the work as a navigable field.
sites.why: Canvas navigation that degrades well.

sites.name: XXIIVV (Devine Lu Linvega)
sites.mechanic: The visitor follows a plain menu or journal, causing linked wiki pages to load in one column, which reveals decades of projects, tools and ethics.
sites.why: Radical restraint with total depth; the opposite pole from WebGL portfolios.

tiers.group: World as navigation · scale as comprehension

sites.name: Radio Garden
sites.mechanic: The visitor rotates the globe and drops onto a dot, causing a live local station to play, which reveals a place through its sound.
sites.why: Navigation by meaningful place instead of menus.

sites.name: neal.fun — The Deep Sea
sites.mechanic: The visitor scrolls down, causing the screen to darken and deeper creatures to pass with depth labels, which reveals how deep the ocean goes.
sites.why: Scroll as a physical quantity — e.g. 3,000 ms vs 15 ms as distance travelled.

sites.name: Collectionscope (AMNH)
sites.mechanic: The visitor moves through a 3D space of 250,000 objects, causing clusters to approach by time and place, which reveals the shape of a collection.
sites.why: Large datasets as places — relevant to Loams and ReviewGraph's graphs.

sites.name: Library of Babel
sites.mechanic: The visitor searches a phrase, causing its exact hexagon/wall/shelf coordinate to load, which reveals that every text already has an address.
sites.why: Addressability as wonder; a content-addressed idea engineers recognise.

sites.name: Smallweb Subway
sites.mechanic: The visitor taps a station, causing its site to open, which reveals webrings as metro lines you can ride.
sites.why: Link structure made spatial and playful.

sites.name: Altis satellite tracker
sites.mechanic: The visitor orbits the globe, causing 10,000+ live satellite positions to shift, which reveals each one's track.
sites.why: Real-time data at scale with restraint (Thailand).

tiers.group: Interfaces that grow · constraint as mechanic

sites.name: A Dark Room
sites.mechanic: The visitor stokes a fire, causing villagers and new tabs to appear, which reveals a larger world behind a one-button start.
sites.why: Progressive disclosure through action — a site that opens as you engage.

sites.name: Universal Paperclips
sites.mechanic: The visitor makes and prices paperclips, causing new panels and scales to unlock, which reveals an optimiser's runaway logic.
sites.why: A system's behaviour told entirely through its own UI state.

sites.name: The Password Game
sites.mechanic: The visitor types a password, causing rules to accumulate and re-check every keystroke, which reveals escalating constraints.
sites.why: Validation as narrative; very legible to engineers.

sites.name: Nothing to Watch
sites.mechanic: The visitor declares their device tier (Potato / Mid-range / High-end), causing the scene to render at that budget, which reveals a graceful answer to uneven hardware.
sites.why: The only site in the audit that asks before it renders.

sites.name: Fabian Tjoe-A-On
sites.mechanic: The visitor arrives without WebGPU, causing the site to explain the requirement and list every project as text, which reveals the work regardless of hardware.
sites.why: The best fallback observed across 67 captures.

sites.name: Making Software
sites.mechanic: The visitor reads a chapter, causing exploded technical illustrations to sit beside the prose, which reveals how familiar hardware and software work.
sites.why: A manual made beautiful; the editorial register an engineer's case study could aim for.

sites.name: The AI Interface Museum
sites.mechanic: The visitor browses a curated collection, causing the history of human–AI interfaces to unfold as exhibits, which reveals a thesis through curation.
sites.why: Curation as authorship — a strong first frame from type alone.

sites.name: Red Blob Games
sites.mechanic: The visitor drags points in diagrams, causing the algorithm's output to redraw, which reveals how it behaves.
sites.why: Algorithms as objects you hold; the gold standard for graph and search explanations.

sites.name: Seeing Theory
sites.mechanic: The visitor runs trials and adjusts parameters, causing distributions to form, which reveals probabilistic behaviour.
sites.why: Statistics made physical — relevant to confidence intervals in FRONTIER.

sites.name: Explorable Multiverse Analyses (Dance)
sites.mechanic: The visitor toggles analysis forks, causing results to jump, which reveals how much an outcome depends on analyst choices.
sites.why: Second example of the same idea; worth reading both.

sites.name: Type in Cube
sites.mechanic: The visitor types any text, causing it to be built from isometric cubes they can style, which reveals type as a 3D object without WebGL spectacle.
sites.why: A tool as a site; strong first frame.

tiers.group: Frontier technique (study the technique, not the first frame)

sites.name: Food for Fish
sites.mechanic: The visitor explores a WebGPU scene, causing generative fish and food systems to respond, which reveals the medium's new ceiling.
sites.why: FWA of the Year 2024; rendered black in software GL.

sites.name: Mingjyun Hung — Still / False Earth
sites.mechanic: The visitor drifts through a generative WebGPU landscape, causing millions of compute-driven grass blades to react, which reveals real-time procedural worlds.
sites.why: The story text survives the GPU error — a partial fallback worth noting.

sites.name: itomdev.com
sites.mechanic: The visitor waits on crumpled paper and a hanging thread, causing the loader itself to read as art direction, which reveals a loader designed as a first frame.
sites.why: If a loader is unavoidable, make it a composition.

sites.name: Mijiheon (Korea)
sites.mechanic: The visitor pulls a jade pendant, causing the gate to open, which reveals an immersive theatre's site in four languages.
sites.why: A tactile gate with cultural meaning, from outside the Anglophone award circuit.
